FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Continuous Bulk Conveying, Elevating, Hoisting, Aerial Ropeways and Related Equipment Sectional 
Committee, had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 

This standard was first published in 1997. Substantial changes in the industrial practices necessitates this revision. 


An aerial ropeway is a special form of transportation system where passengers/materials are carried on atensioned 
wire rope supported above the ground. Aerial ropeways are particularly useful in regions wherethe facility in 
surmounting natural barriers gives them a great advantage over railways or roads, both ofwhich may need the 
heavy civil engineering work to secure easy gradient. They are inexpensive to maintain, their power demand is 
modest and not seriously affected by adverse climatic conditions. 


Nothing in this standard is intended to contravene any provisions of the statutory regulations wherever they are 
in force. 


The major changes in this revision are as follows: 
a) Scope has been modified; 
b 


c) Latest constructional materials as per relevant Indian Standards have been mentioned for construction of 
material handling ropeways; 


wm 


Terminology has been modified; 


d) Factor of safety for design of ropeway has been defined in this Standard; and 
e) Clause on trestles, carriers, stations and safety requirements has been added in this Standard. 


Annex A gives a list of standards which may be used in the design and construction of aerial ropeways. This list, 
although not exhaustive, includes standards on raw materials like steels, structural sections, equipment, such 
as motors, wire ropes, bearings, components of aerial ropeways, fasteners, design parameters, etc. This list is 
also expected to help the user of an aerial ropeway in the procurement of quality product for use during the 
maintenance of the aerial ropeways. 


Composition of the Panel-1 on ‘Aerial Ropeways’ of MED 06 responsible for the formulation of this standard is 
given at Annex B. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of the standard is complied with the value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised )’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off values should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 9706 : 2019 


Indian Standard 


MATERIAL HANDLING ROPEWAYS — 
CODE OF PRACTICE 


( Second Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


1.1 This Standard covers the design and construction 
of all types and systems of material handling ropeways, 
except the cases where goods are transported by 
passenger ropeways. 


1.2 This standard does not apply to ropeways used in 
agriculture and forestry. 


2 REFERENCES 


The Standards listed in Annex A contain provisions 
which, through reference in the text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to make agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards. 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the terminology given 
in IS 7649 and the following shall apply. 


3.1 Ropeway with Automatic Grip — Continuous 
movement aerial ropeways with automatic grip in 
which the carrier are automaticallycoupled to the rope 
on leaving the station and detached on arrival at the 
station. 


3.2 Line — Route alignment of the ropeway between 
two terminals. 


3.3 Inspecting Authority — Competent authority 
recognized by the statutory regulations to inspect 
the aerial ropeways installation and determine its 
acceptability or otherwise, on the basis of this standard 
and compliance to prevailing statutory rules and 
regulations. 


4 GENERAL DESIGN REQUIREMENTS 


4.1 Guidelines for Design and Construction 


4.1.1 Each part of the ropeway equipment shall be 
designed and constructed in conformity with this 
standard and also all technical considerations to ensure 
full and safe working of the ropeway.The quality of 
the materials to be used for its construction shall be 
as per the design. All the materials used shall meet 


with the requirements laid down in the relevant Indian 
Standards. A list of relevant Indian Standards is given 
in Annex A. 


4.1.2 On the request of the supervising authorities or of 
the purchaser, test certificates (from statutory accredited 
testing lab) shall be supplied by the constructor as 
regards the characteristics of all material used and 
essential to the safety of the installation. 


4.1.3 All moving parts of the ropeway, which can be 
dangerous to the operating personnel, shall be suitably 
guarded or fenced off. 


4.1.4 All parts of ropeway that require frequent 
servicing and maintenance shall have free access. 


4.1.5 All parts of the ropeway plant shall be protected 
against corrosion. 


4.1.6 Line sheaves and saddles shall be made of steel. 


4.1.7 Maximum and minimum temperatures and 
weather conditions for a particular ropeway area shall 
be given due consideration when designing a ropeway. 


4.2 Route and Profile of the Ropeway 


4.2.1 As a rule, the axis of the line in its plan position 
shall be straight. However, horizontal deviation of 
the path of the travel may be permitted as regards 
supporting trestles provided that: 


a) For Monocable Ropeways — Minimum load on 
a trestle is equal to the weight of the rope on the 
trestle plus 150 kg and the angle of horizontal 
deviation does not exceed 0.5 degree (0.9 percent). 
This effect shall not be cumulative. 


b 


wm 


For Bicable Ropeways — Deviation of up to 
1.14 degree (two percent) per support may be 
permitted provided the supports are located in a 
very gentle arc having a minimum radius of 5.0 m. 


4.2.2 For bicable installation, the minimum angle 
of vertical deflection of rope over a line trestle, with 
the maximum tension in the rope and the rope only 
condition, shall not be less than 1 percent when the 
sum of the two adjacent spans is equal to or less than 
200 metres, and not less than 1.25 percent when the 
sum of the spans is greater than 200 metres. 


IS 9706 : 2019 


4.2.3 The maximum angle of rope deflection over 
a line trestle shall not exceed the values for which 
the saddles and line-sheaves batteries have been 
designed. 


4.2.4 If the Length of a ropeway is too long, it may be 
divided in multiple sections having independent Drive, 
and in the case of a bi-cable rope way track rope divide 
stations are considered. 


4.2.5 The length between track rope divide-tension 
stations is determined by the cumulative tension due to 
the difference of levels and the friction resistance force 
on the saddles and also transportation and handling 
aspects.The rope friction can be taken into account with 
a friction coefficient of 0.10. 


The increase in tension should not be greater than 
25 percent of the tension weight load. 


4.2.6 Length of the hauling rope section shall be 
decided on the basis of the actual design requirements 
based on system capacity, terrain, workability etc., 
provided that using standard criteria, different safety 
aspect of the hauling rope lay down in appropriate 
standards are adhered to. 


4.2.7 In cases, when the straight line profile crosses 
too many obstacles in the form of built-up areas, 
roads, rivers, densely inhabited area etc., an alternative 
straight route or a route with angle stations should be 
considered. 


4.2.8 All crossing points of roads, railways and 
power lines etc., shall be discussed and agreed upon 
by the purchaser and appropriate authorities. Crossings 
should be protected by bridges or protection nets 
(see 4.5). 


4.2.9 The carriers must be capable of passing over 
the trestles even in presence of inward and outward 
oscillation of 12° with minimum 0.25 m clearance 
without contact with tower structure. 


4.2.10 In order to ensure free movement of carriers 
in the station, the side clearance between the space 
occupied by the carrier and fixed obstacles belonging to 
the installation shall be not less than 0.20 m measured 
towards the interior of the line and 1 m measured 
towards the outside. If the carrier are not guided, these 
values shall be maintained even when the carrier is 
inclined transversely at 12°. 


4.2.11 Along the line, the distance between the two 
paths of travel of the rope (track width), shall be such as 
to ensure a clearance of at least 0.4 m between carrier 
swung by 12° towards one another. Such clearance is 
required for spans having a length of not more than 
200 m. As for longer spans, the clearance shall be 
increased by 0.10 m for each additional 100 m or 
fraction thereof. 


4.2.12 Aminimum clearance of 30 cm between the space 
occupied by a loaded carrier, swung longitudinally by 
15° and obstacles lying on the vertical longitudinal 
plane, shall be ensured either along the line or in the 
stations. 


4.2.13 The minimum vertical clearance, that is, the 
distance between the ground with obstacles existing 
over it, such as trees, rocks, snow drifts etc. and the 
lowest moving portion of a ropeway (bottom of the 
bucket or haulage rope) (also see 4.5.2.2) shall be as 
given below, under the most unfavorable conditions or 
assuming a conventional increase of 20 percent of the 
amount of static sag, shall be not less than: 


a) Over National highways 6.0m 
b) Over other vehicular roads 4.5m 
c) Over footpaths frequented by 

pedestrians 2.5m 
d) Over areas where traffic is not 

allowed to pass 1.5m 


The minimum clearances are normally not available at 
entry and exit points of the carriers from the stations. 
Such places shall be cordoned off by fencing. 


4.2.14 In case of crossings with overhead electric 
lines, railway lines, navigational passage, net clearance 
shall be as specified in respective statutory provisions. 
These clearances shall be under the most unfavorable 
conditions. 


4.3 Maximum 
Between Carriers 


Speed and Minimum Spacing 


4.3.1 The maximum speed adopted for the system 
shall be consistent with safe working of all mechanical 
elements and shall not induce abnormal loads in the 
rope or any other part of the system. 


In no case shall the maximum speed exceed the values 
given below: 


a) Continuously circulating 


bicable ropeways - 5.0 m/sec 
b) To-and-fro bicable ropeways - 8.0 m/sec 
c) Continuously circulatingmonocable 

ropeways - 4.5 m/sec 
d) To-and-fro monocable ropeways - 6.0 m/sec 


The drive shall also be capable of running the system at 
inspection speed, that is, 0.3-0.5 m/s and traversing the 
carrier a full cycle. 


4.3.2 In case the stations are not provided with 
mechanism for regulating the release of carriers on the 
line as per designed interval, it shall be ensured that 
under no circumstances, the distance separating two 
successive carrier shall be less than 1 m, considering 
15° longitudinal swing of two carrier towards each 
other under the conditions of emergency stopping. 


4.4 Rope Guiding 


4.4.1 The permanency of the carrying wire rope on the 
shoes shall be ensured even under the most unfavourable 
conditions. The minimum load on the shoe shall be at 
least 50 percent greater than the force which would be 
necessary to unseat the rope taking into account a gust 
of wind as per IS 875. 


4.4.2 Track rope line saddles shall be such mounted 
that they are free to oscillate and their shape is such 
that the carriage pass over them smoothly. The radius of 
the rope groove on a saddle shall be 10 percent larger 
than the rope radius. The minimum radius of a saddle 
shall not be less than 100 times rope diameter or 
3 500 mm. 


4.4.3 In bicable ropeways with the under type system 
carriage, provisions shall be made to guide the hauling 
rope on to the supporting rollers. 


4.4.4 The minimum load on a trestle for monocable 
ropeways shall be equal to the weight of the rope on the 
trestle plus 150 kg. 


4.4.5 On monocable ropeways, all the line sheaves 
should have ball or roller bearings and all the oscillating 
mounts shall have bushes of cast iron, bronze, nylon or 
other suitable material. 


4.4.6 On trestles, two sheaves on each side of the line 
are minimum. Single sheaves are not allowed except 
for the rope lead on the driving or return sheaves. 


4.5 Crossing with Traffic Lines 
4.5.1 General 


a) The crossings and paralleling with railways, 
highways, ropeways or overhead electrical 
lines shall be so done that no mutual discomfort 
results either in course of normal operation or 
during installation operations. Wherever the local 
conditions are favourable and the characteristics of 
the electrical line permit it, the overhead electrical 
lines shall be grounded in conformity with 
prevalent statutory regulations. If underground 
cabling is not possible, ropeway shall pass 
below it. 


b 


wm 


All heavy traffic lines (railways, roads and 
industrial areas) shall have protective structures. 


c) All other traffic paths (connecting tracks, field 
paths, etc.) shall have warning boards. 


d) At the place of crossing with railways, the 
protective structures shall be designed to offer 
protection against a falling ropeway carrier. In 
the case of crossing with roads and industrial 
areas, the protective structures shall be designed 
to offer protection against falling material, that is 
conveyed and falling of the ropes. 


IS 9706 : 2019 


e) The protection bridges shall be made of 
steel, concrete, wood, guard net or a suitable 
combination of these. Suitably painted yellow/ 
black stripes warning boards shall be provided on 
them. 


4.5.2 Protection Bridges 


4.5.2.1 The surface of the protective bridges shall be 
located as close as possible toand below the lower edge 
of ropeway carrier under most unfavorable conditions 
in case of ropeway passing above the obstruction. In 
case of ropeway passing under the high tension line 
the clearance shall be measured from the highest point 
in the ropeway carriage. The width of the protective 
bridges shall be such that, even if a side swing of 
12 degree occurs, the car and parts that fall from it can 
be securely caught. 


4.5.2.2 Top level of the deck or net shall be such that 
the moving carriers, even if two numbers are bunched, 
shall not touch or hit, under the worst conditions of sag, 
a bucket fallen on its sides (or bucket and hanger) left 
uncleared on the deck. 


4.5.2.3 The clearances under the protective bridges 
shall be as specified in 4.2.13 and 4.2.14. 


4.5.2.4 The load due to dead weight, snow and wind 
shall be taken in accordance with relevant Indian 
Standards. A list of relevant Indian Standards is given 
in Annex A. 


4.5.2.5 If a fall of a carrier has to be taken into account, 
then the non-elastic impact of its heaviest single 
part (carriage or hanger or bucket together with the 
conveyed material) shall be taken into account for 
the calculation of the directly hit supporting structure 
(covering, transverse beam). If only falling material 
that is conveyed has to be taken into account, then this 
shall be done by assuming a static load of 100 kg/m? 
over the entire bridge. 


4.5.2.6 The metal parts of the trestle shall have a factor 
of safety defined as the ratio of the ultimate strength 
of the metal to stress in the metal under the most 
unfavourable conditions of not less than 3.0 when the 
installation is in service. 


4.5.3 Protective or Guard Net 


4.5.3.1 The guard net shall be located below the lower 
edge of the ropeway carrier and as near to it as possible. 


4.5.3.2 The guard net shall be supported by 3 or 4 
carrying ropes anchored securely at both ends or 
tensioned by weights on one side. 


4.5.3.3 For short nets a series of buffer springs shall be 
provided in all cases at each of the two, carrying rope 
ends in order to assure moderate tension increase in the 
carrying rope if a carrier falls. 


IS 9706 : 2019 


4.5.3.4 For binding the carrying rope in the region of 
the net, steel cross bars shall be located at 3 to 4 m 
distance. 


4.5.3.5 To prevent objects fallen on the net from rolling 
sideward, the ends of the cross bars shall be bent up by 
60° over a length of one meter. 


4.5.3.6 The bent up ends of the cross bars shall be 
connected by a railing rope. 


4.5.3.7 Once the lattice is formed of ropes and cross 
bars, two galvanized steel wire nets shall be placed 
on it. The first net shall be of steel wires of minimum 
3 mm diameter and 3 to 8 cm mesh width. Over 
this a second net of fine mesh with 1 to 2 cm width, 
according to the type of material conveyed, shall be 
placed. 


4.5.3.8 The nets shall be fastened with strong galvanized 
binding wires to the suspension ropes, the railing ropes 
and the cross bars. 


4.5.3.9 The wind and snow load shall be considered in 
accordance with relevant Indian standards. 


4.5.3.10 While considering a falling carrier, the load 
assumption and the safety factor shall be in accordance 
with 4.5.2.6. 


4.6 Dangerous Areas 


4.6.1 In the proximity of airports or in areas where 
aeroplanes fly at low altitude or land frequently, the 
route of the ropeway shall be adequately marked, taking 
into account any restriction imposed by the Authority 
having jurisdiction over the airports. 


4.6.2 The areas exposed to the dangers of natural forces 
(avalanches, landslides, rock falls, storms, etc.) shall be 
avoided as far as possible. 


4.6.3 When the dangers indicated in 4.6.2 exist, suitable 
protection devices shall be provided. 


4.7 Wind Action 


4.7.1 The wind forces and their effects (static 
and dynamic) shall be taken into account, when 
designing ropeways. The provisions mentioned 
in IS 875 (Part 3) and in IS 802 (Part 1) shall be 
followed. 


4.7.2 In the calculation of wind action on cables, the 
surface area to be considered shall be the 


diameteral surface of the cable multiplied by the 
factor (Cw): 

a) Cw = 1.1 for snow bound areas; and 

b) Cw = 0.7 for areas not affected by snow. 


4.7.3 The uplift caused by breeze/wind on wire rope and 
carrier considered along with the conditions specified 
in 4.4 shall be fully met. 


5 ROPES 


5.1 Construction 


Rope construction shall be such selected which is 
best suited for its intended function. For track ropes 
of bicableropeway, ropes of full or half-locked 
coil construction is recommended. For hauling and 
carrying-hauling ropes, it shall be of the stranded 
construction having a fibre core or plastic core, Lang.’s 
lay. Tensioning ropes shall be of the ordinary lay 
(crossed lay) stranded construction. 


Ropes and connecting equipment shall conform to 
the relevant Indian standards. A list of such Indian 
standards is given in Annex A. 


5.2 Factor of Safety 


At maximum load during service, the factor of safety, 
that is, the ratio of minimum breaking load of rope and 
the maximum rope tension in service shall not be less 
than the following values: 


Carrying rope (bicable) 3.0 
Hauling rope for both monocable 

and bicable 4.5 
Tension rope for bicable and monocable 5.0 
Signalling and telephonic cables 3.3 


5.3 Splices and Rope Termination 


5.3.1 For track ropes, the ends shall be connected by 
means of coupling sockets with wedges or filled-in 
with alloy material. 


The ends of the tensioning ropes shall be mounted in 
sockets filled-in with alloy material, however, on small 
capacity ropeways fixing with bull dog clamps shall be 
allowed. 


5.3.1.1 Haulage or carrying 


Hauling rope shall be spliced over a length not less than 
1 200 times and the distance between two splices shall 
be not less than 3 000 times the diameter of the rope. 


5.3.2 Splicing and rope socketing shall be done with 
utmost care. Only organization or person having 
adequate experience in splicing and rope sockets shall 
be entrusted with the job. 


5.4 Discard Criteria of Ropes 


Generally a rope should be withdrawn from service 
when it is considered that: 


a) for track ropes, if the diametrical cross-section 
is reduced by 15 percent or more due to wear or 
corrosion or loosening of wires over a length of 


200 times the diameter of rope. It shall also be 
discarded, if, over a length of 1.0 m there are more 
than 5 outer wire breakages; 


b 


wm 


the loss of strength in the rope due to fatigue, 
surface embrittlement or cracked and broken 
wiresof any kind is 20 percent or more or if the 
factor of safety has decreased by | 5percent of the 
value when the rope was first installed, or if one 
of the strands is completely severed: 


c) the outer wires have lost about one-third of their 
depth as a result of any kind of deterioration; 


d) the outer wires are becoming loose and displaced 
for any reason; 


e) the rope has become kinked, distorted or damaged 
and the damaged piece cannot be removed; 


f) examination of the rope leaves any doubt as to its 
safety for any reason what-so-ever; and 


g) the number of wires rupture in the rope exceed the 
limit specified in 8.1.6 of IS 3973. 


6 LOADS ON SHEAVES, DRUMS AND 
SADDLES 


6.1 Normal Load 


6.1.1 The number of carriage rollers shall be such that 
the maximum load on any one of them does not exceed 
one-eightieth of the minimum tension for the carrying 
rope at the point considered. It is recommended that a 
ratio between the normal load in the cable produced 
by the carrier and the minimum tension of the carrying 
cable not exceeding one-twelfth this adopted. 


6.1.2 For normal loads in moving wire ropes, the 
requirements of 4.4 shall be taken into account. 


6.1.3 Sheaves, Drums and Shoe 


The fixed drum to which the anchorage of carrying 
ropes are secured by friction shall have a diameter 
of not less than 65 times that of the wire rope and 
1 000 times that of the outer wires of the wire ropes. 
The wire rope shall make at least three rounds of the 
drum and it should be served at least by two fasteners at 
the outlet, of which one assures the proper fixation and 
the second serves to check the slip of the wire rope, if 
any, and functions as the safety device. 


6.1.3.1 The diameter of the pulleys of the tensioning 
devices to which the carrying ropes fixed directly to the 
counter weights shall be at least 100 times that of the 
wire rope. 


6.1.3.2 The radius of the roller and returns for 
tensioning the wire ropes fixed directly to the counter 
weights shall be not less than 100 times that of the 
wire ropes and1 200 times that of the wires of the wire 
ropes. 


IS 9706 : 2019 


6.1.3.3 The diameter of deflection pulleys of stranded 
stretch wire rope shall be not less than 40 times that 
of the wire rope and at least 600 times that of the wire 
in the outer layer of the wire rope. These pulleys shall 
be provided with linings in leather, wood or any other 
relatively soft material. 


6.1.3.4 The diameter of the driving and return sheaves 
shall be not less than 80 times that of the hauling rope 
and at least 800 times that of the wires of the wire rope. 


6.1.3.5 The support saddles which support the carrying 
rope shall present such a profile that while passing the 
trestles any danger or sliding of carrier is avoided. They 
have to ensure the equilibrium tension in the wire rope 
and to permit free displacement of the wire rope in 
the longitudinal direction when necessary, by making 
use of the rollers. The radius of curvature of saddle 
supports shall be at least 100 times that of the wire rope 
diameter. 


7 TRESTLES 


7.1 Loads 


In designing trestles, the following stress values shall 
be taken into account: 


a) The weight of the trestle and the pressure exerted 
by the ropes; 

b) The whole of the stresses due to friction met with 
during the motion of the moving ropes and during 
the displacement of a stationary rope; 


c) Weight of the carrier travelling with maximum 
load (considered conventionally static load); 


d) Wind load or snow load; and 


e) Load imposed by communication cable, if 
provided. 


7.1.1 The wind forces and their effects (static and 
dynamic) should be taken into account when designing 
trestles. The provisions mentioned in IS 875 (Part 3), 
IS 802 (Part 1) shall be followed. Further, loads due 
to snow in accordance with IS 875 (Part 4) shall also 
be considered. The design shall also consider seismic 
loads in accordance with IS 1893. In addition, other 
special loads in accordance with IS 875 (Part 5) shall 
also be considered. 


7.2 Safety 


7.2.1 The metal parts of the trestle shall have a safety 
factor defined as the ratio of the ultimate strength of the 
metal to stress in the metal under the most unfavourable 
conditions of not less than 2.0 when the installation is 
in service. 


7.2.2 The trestle shall be analyzed and designed for 
various load combinations as per IS 802. The trestle 


IS 9706 : 2019 


foundation shall be either a shallow foundation or deep 
foundation or founded on rock anchors. 


7.2.3 The elastic deformation of the trestles, in 
particular those due to torsion which happens during 
normal conditions of operation, shall not be, such as to 
endanger the stability of the ropes. The maximum angle 
of deformation due to torsion shall be limited in such 
a manner that the ends of the shoes for supporting the 
carrying-hauling rope are not displaced by more than 
20 percent of the wire rope diameter. 


7.3 Construction 


7.3.1 The number of trestles, their position, their 
height and their construction are determined by the 
requirements of the route and the layout. Wooden 
trestles or trestles which are guyed shall not be used. 


7.3.2 In case the trestles have metallic framework, the 
thickness of the open profile shape shall not be less than 
5 mm while in the case of closed profile, it shall not 
be less than 2.5 mm. The interior of the latter shall be 
adequately protected against corrosion. 


7.3.3 The anchorage of the trestles on the concrete 
foundations or on the rock shall be carefully made. 
The anchor bolts of concrete foundations shall just be 
atleast 300 mm above natural ground level. 


8 CARRIER 


8.1 Carriages 

a) The carriers shall be so designed that safe transport 
of material is ensured. 

b) The carriage wheel load shall include the maximum 
clip pressure due to the haulage rope arising out 
of maximum break over angle of haulage rope at 
grip, on the line. 

c 


wm 


Prevention of any accidental unlocking of carriage 
grip shall be ensured. It shall also be ensured that 
the rope is gripped efficiently even if the rope 
diameter is reduced by 15 percent. 


d) At maximum slope of the ropeway, under the 
most unfavourable friction conditions, a minimum 
safety factor of 1.5 shall be maintained against 
slippage between the hauling rope and the grip. 
If only one grip is used for attaching the carrier 
to the carrying-hauling rope, it shall be capable 
of offering resistance to sliding at least equal to 
twice the component of the loaded carrier weighed 
along the axis of the wire rope and the maximum 
slope and in no case, this resistance to sliding be 
less than that of the loadedcarrier. 


e 


wa 


For monocableropeway, the form of the grip and 
the profile of the grooves of the trestle roller shall 
be adapted to one another, taking into account 
specially the maximum lateral swing permitted for 


the carrier. As also the carriers pass over the trestle 
sheaves without bumping. 

f) For fixed-grip systems (Jig-back ropeways), it 
must be possible for the grips to be easily shifted 
periodically. 


an 


The carrier shall be suspended in such a manner 
that whatever be the slope of the track, the bucket 
remains suspended in the vertical position. 


8 


8.2 Inspection and Lubrication Car 


It is recommended that each bi-cable ropeway is 
equipped with an inspection car for line inspection and 
a lubricating car for the track rope lubrication 


8.3 Numbering 


In order to distinguish the carriers on the line, they shall 
be successively numbered. 


9 STATIONS 


9.1 General 


9.1.1 Station layouts shall be such that their intended 
function like loading, unloading, parking, maintenance 
can be effectively and safely carried out. 


9.1.2 The station machinery, such as mechanical parts 
of the driving gear, tension gear, electrical equipment, 
ropes and carriers shall not be a source of danger to the 
rope way operators and trespassers. 


9.1.3 Engine room, operator’s desk, electrical 
equipment, tension device etc. shall be guarded against 
entry /access by unauthorized personnel. 


9.1.4 The whole of the driving gear and of the return 
or deflection devices shall be protected against bad 
weather. 


9.1.5 Fire hazard shall be reduced as far as possible. Fire 
extinguishers as per local area regulations guaranteed to 
function effectively shall be kept ready in case of need 
and installed in places which are readily accessible. 


9.1.6 For the calculation of the station structure 
the provisions of the relevant Indian Standards as 
applicable to industrial buildings shall be applicable in 
addition to those required for ropeway. 


9.1.7 For calculating the load for the bearing structure 
of the overhead shunt rails and for the rails themselves, 
it shall be assumed that fully loaded carriages are one 
behind the other. 


9.2 Driving and Braking 


9.2.1 Starting of the system even under the most 
unfavourable conditions of load shall be guaranteed. 


9.2.2 In the case of downward load, the driver itself 
shall exert a continuous braking action. 


9.2.3 Travel with the main motor shall be stopped 
automatically when any brake is on or if any safety 
device operates. 


9.2.4 Rope Adhesion on the Driving Sheave 


9.2.4.1 The friction coefficient (u) between the rope 
and the surface of the groove of the driving sheave are 
as follows: 


a) Groove without lining 


(cast iron or steel) : u = 0.07 
b) Groove with leather lining >p=0.15 
c) Groove with rubber or similar >p=0.25 
material with high friction coefficient 
d) Groove with aluminum lining > p= 0.20 


9.2.4.2 The contact angle of the rope on the driving 
sheave shall be such as to ensure that in the most 
unfavourable combination of circumstances the 
required power is transmitted to the rope. In cases, 
when drive power is very high, Karlik grip type 
gripping sheave may be used. 


9.2.5 Braking 


9.2.5.1 Each drive shall be equipped with two brakes 
acting independently of each other. One of these shall 
be automatic with provision for manual release. One 
brake shall act directly on the driving sheave. It can 
be a handbrake provided the other brake, acting on 
gearbox input shaft, is automatic. Jig-back ropeways 
and installation which stops on its own without the 
application of any external brake, can have only one 
brake but it should act automatically when the ropeway 
stops. 


9.2.5.2 The factor of safety against required braking 
power shall be not less than 1.5. 


9.3 Rope Tensioning and Anchorage Devices 


9.3.1 Hauling ropes and carrying-hauling ropes shall 
be tensioned by tension weight or other suitable 
tensioning devices. Tension in track ropes shall be 
provided by tension weight. 


9.3.2 The spaces in which the counterweights travel 
(in pit or construction above the ground) shall be 
protected from water, snow, and ice and from any other 
material. It shall be ensured that the above elements do 
not accumulate inside these spaces. These spaces shall 
be provided with guard-rails in order to prevent the 
entrance of unauthorized persons. 


9.3.3 The mobility of the counter weights shall be 
ensured at all times. 


9.3.4 The travel of the counterweight shall be 
determined taking into account the maximum 
variation which may be due to the sag of each span, 
the surrounding temperature of the zone where the 


IS 9706 : 2019 


installation lies (minimum variation to be considered 
is 60°) and the elastic stretch of the rope.The distance 
of travel for tension weights and tension trolley shall 
be limited by stops. Provision of limit switches may be 
there to stop the system automatically in the event they 
reach their extreme position. 


9.3.5 The tension weights shall have guides to arrest 
swinging and twisting of weight block. 


9.3.6 In cases when track ropes are fixed by 
anchorage’s on both ends, provision must be made for 
measuring and regulation of the tension in the rope. 


9.3.7 Where several tensioning ropes are laid in 
parallel, all the necessary precautions shall be taken 
in order to ensure uniform distribution of the tension 
among such ropes. 


9.3.8 In place of tension ropes, chains can be used. 
The safety factor shall be at least 5 in this case. Other 
systems are permissible subject to agreement between 
the ropeway promoter and the inspecting authority. 


9.3.9 The foundations of either tensioning devices or 
anchorage shall have a factor of safety of 1.5 in respect 
of shifting and over turning. Such factor of safety is to 
be calculated on the basis of a conventional assumption 
that these foundations are free, that is, there is no lateral 
movement of the earth. 


9.3.10 All foundations shall be in accordance with 
relevant Indian Standards listed in Annex A. 


10 SAFETY REQUIREMENT 


10.1 Emergency stop buttons shall be provided at 
suitable location at all stations . Re-starting shall be 
allowed only after removing the fault. 


10.2 Automatic Stopping of the ropeway shall be 
ensured in the event of any of the following: 


a) supply voltage drops below the minimum 
specified, 

b) supply voltage increases above the maximum 
specified, 

c) designed speed of ropeway is exceeds by 
10 percent, and 


d) one of the safety switches is activated. 


10.3 System with detachable grip shall have suitable 
bucket spacing arrangement before leaving the station. 


10.4 Jig-back ropeways shall be equipped with limit 
stops and buffers that will stop the system in the case 
when the distance of travel is exceeded. 


10.5 Ropeways shall be provided with dedicated 
telephone installation between the stations. Portable 
telephones or wireless sets shall be available with line 
inspecting team.

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards: Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: MED 06 (13427).
